summary: Architecture for local task manager web app

sections.requirements: Provide a local task manager web app (HTML/JS) without backend, using localStorage.
sections.options: 1. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with localStorage. 2. React or Vue framework with localStorage.
sections.simplest_viable: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with localStorage. No build tools, no frameworks, zero dependencies.
sections.tradeoffs: Vanilla JS is simpler but may become harder to maintain if complexity grows. Frameworks offer maintainability but violate the simplest_viable constraint due to build overhead.
sections.financial_feasibility: $0 operational cost. Runs entirely locally on the client's browser.
sections.security: Data never leaves the client device. Primary risk is XSS, which must be mitigated by properly escaping task input before rendering in the DOM.
sections.adr: ADR-001: Use Vanilla HTML/JS and localStorage to adhere to strict simplicity and zero backend constraints.
sections.risks: Data loss if user clears browser storage. Storage quota limitations (~5MB), though unlikely to be reached for simple text tasks.
